question: How does an operating system handle a page fault?

passages.text: A page fault causes a trap into the kernel, which checks the virtual address and may load the missing page from backing storage.
The CPU scheduler selects a runnable process according to the scheduling policy.
The page fault handler resolves missing virtual memory mappings before allowing execution to resume.

question: How does TCP ensure packets are delivered in order?

passages.text: TCP uses sequence numbers to reconstruct the original byte stream even when network segments arrive out of order.
UDP provides datagram delivery without guaranteeing ordered delivery.
The receiver uses sequence information to reorder incoming TCP segments.
